title: Square-zero algebra lifting criterion for vanishing cotangent modules
statement: Let $R$ and $A$ be commutative rings and let $R\to A$ give $A$ an $R$-algebra structure. Write $\Omega_{A/R}$ for the module of Kähler differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] and $H_1(L_{A/R})$ for the first homology of the naive cotangent complex [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Then $\Omega_{A/R}=0$ and $H_1(L_{A/R})=0$ if and only if, for every commutative $R$-algebra $D$, every ideal $I\subseteq D$ with $I^2=0$, and every $R$-algebra homomorphism $u:A\to D/I$, there exists exactly one $R$-algebra homomorphism $v:A\to D$ with $q\circ v=u$, where $q:D\to D/I$ is the quotient map. No finite-generation or finite-presentation hypothesis is imposed on $A$.

mathlib_match.how: Exact after expanding Algebra.FormallyEtale by Algebra.formallyEtale_iff, generated by @[mk_iff] on lines 46-49: Subsingleton of each module means that it is zero. The theorem at lines 86-95 says precisely that all quotient-composition maps on R-algebra homomorphisms are bijective. Bijectivity is the stated existence and uniqueness for each u. No finite-presentation hypothesis; the universe max u v in its test algebra is the usual common-universe formulation.
